design:
D1. "The same failure" is the same pytest node ids, compared like for like (owner: project_checks.py, which already owns what a check result means). Today a failure is rerun once with the gate's own options (narrowed_command keeps `-n auto`, :598-626) and then the whole check is run on main, whose exit code alone decides `preexisting` (:713-726). New order for a failing check whose ids pytest named in full (failed_test_ids, :580-595): (1) rerun only those ids on the task's tree, serially (`-n` value set to 0, `--dist`, `--maxprocesses`, `--tx` dropped; a command without `-n` is already serial); all pass -> flaky, the check passes as today; (2) otherwise run the same serial narrowed command on main at the run's main_sha; each id that fails there is shared, each that passes is the task's own. The result stores on_main.failed_tests, shared_tests, own_tests and touched_tests. A check without named ids keeps today's whole-check baseline and check-level `preexisting`, which is never automatic. Why one serial rerun: the night's test passed one narrowed rerun and failed the next under `-n auto` while another suite ran; serial removes the load it creates for itself, and one attempt keeps a reproducible own failure from being retried into a pass, as today. Why narrowed on main: the same command on both trees is the comparison; a whole-suite main run (8-18 min that night) answers a different question.

D2. Never automatic for the task's own (owner: project_checks records, requirement_gate decides). Excluded: any own id; any failing or flaky id whose file (the node id's path part) is in changed_paths(main_sha, merged) (:144); on a Hub-filed fix task, the ids it was filed for; checks without named ids, timeouts, more than MAX_RERUN_TESTS (50); a missing main answer (_MainBaseline.unavailable). A flaky test in a file the task changed now fails the run instead of passing: the one place this slice tightens the gate, because a task that adds a flaky test introduced it.

D3. The override is decided where overrides are decided today and recorded where they are recorded (owner: requirement_gate._check_checks, :1081-1139, and task_transition_service.apply_transition, :903-971). _check_checks gains a third outcome beside 'refuse' and 'operator override': when the setting is on and every failure in the run is shared or flaky and none is excluded, it sets refusal.automatic_override (the checks, ids, kinds, run id, main sha, fix task id) and does not refuse. apply_transition writes override_reason from it with override_by 'hub' when the operator gave no reason; an operator's typed reason still wins and records override_by 'operator'. The actor stays the approver: actor kinds are run and operator only (task_transitions.py:34-36) and models.py:874-879 records the decision that the Hub acting is not a third actor kind, so 'who overrode' is a column of its own, not an actor. approval_held_for_operator asks evaluate (:1403), so the mender's hold disappears with the refusal and needs no change. The reviewer briefing (review_turn.py:560-567) reads the same decision instead of telling the reviewer to send the task back.

D4. One project setting, on by default (owner: Project, beside `checks`, models.py:127; ProjectSettings in api/v1/projects.py:123-170). `checks_auto_override` governs the automatic override and fix-task filing together; off is exactly today. Slice D later replaces it with a per-level rule; keeping one switch now avoids inventing levels here.

D5. The fix task is filed when the run ends, not at approval (owner: flaky_tests.py, widened from 'flaky tests the checks found' to 'failures the checks found that are not the task's'). At run end the Hub knows the failure is main's or a flake, the flow's agents are often idle waiting on the held task (2026-10-27), and approval's transaction stays free of task creation (create_task_for_actor commits, api/v1/tasks.py:868-890). Filed through create_task_for_actor with operator authority, as api/v1/checks.py:59-66 already does for flakes. Deduplicated by test id against open Hub-filed fix tasks, recorded as event_logs rows the way flaky_tests records 'handled' (no new task column). Text reuses fix_task_text for flakes and a sibling for main's failures (check, ids, main sha, run, failure excerpt, 'done when these ids pass on main').

D6. 'Head of the flow' is priority (owner: scheduler._loop_queue_order, :590-614, shared with the board so they cannot disagree). Pending tasks order by priority rank (critical, high, medium, low) before created_at; the fix task is critical. Task.priority already exists with those values (schemas/tasks.py:57) and is used by nothing in the queue; spec materialisation writes medium (spec_tasks.py:415), so a spec flow's order is unchanged. Rejected: a dedicated 'head' flag (a second ordering field), and making the fix task a prerequisite of the remaining tasks (it would hold them, the opposite of the point). The flow is the held task's own loop when live (flow_advance.py:118-128's test); otherwise the fix task is pending and unassigned, visible on the board.

D7. An assigned task outside a flow is started by one rule with several nudges (owner: new hub/hub/assigned_task_start.py, modelled on flow_advance's after-commit hook, flow_advance.py:50-53, :139-151). Rule: status assigned, loop_id null, assignee an open agent, dependency gate clear, and no entry with this task_id for this assignee queued, delivered or running since the task's latest move to assigned. Action: queue one entry bound to the task (task_id set, so the runtime moves it to in_progress as on 2026-10-27 at 02:56), origin 'operator', or 'agent' with origin_agent when an agent's run assigned it (no new origin type, so no CHECK-constraint rebuild of inbound_queue_entries), briefing = title, id, description and scheduler._briefing_completion_lines(task, is_flow=False); then turn_scheduler.schedule_agent. Nudged after commit by apply_transition (-> assigned), create_task_for_actor (created assigned) and update_task (new assignee while assigned); the stall sweep (stalls.py:65, every 300 s) runs the same rule for the project as the backstop. 'Since it entered assigned' is what stops a re-queue spin when a delivered turn ended without starting the task; that case is a divergence, already recorded elsewhere. Pending tasks with an assignee are not started: assigned is the operator's 'work this now'.

Hazard. (1) Policy: work now reaches main over red checks without the operator. Bounded by D1-D2 (ids must fail on main too, or pass alone; never a test the task touched), recorded on every such transition, and switched off per project by D4. (2) Migration 0148 (next free number at build time; slices C and K also add migrations): add task_transitions.override_by String(16) nullable, backfilled 'operator' where override_reason is not null; add projects.checks_auto_override Boolean not null server_default true. Runs on the operator's :8000 data at its next restart (authorised 2026-10-27; back up first with the mode=ro backup in .claude/reference/hubs.md). Rollback: downgrade drops both columns in batch mode; automatic overrides then read as operator overrides whose reason text says the Hub made them, and nothing else is lost. The operational rollback needs no code: turn the setting off. (3) The UI bundle commit reaches :8000 on its next reload; ship it with the backend that serves override_by and the setting.

open_questions.question: The roadmap's non-goal reads 'at every level red checks mean no merge'. Do flakes also get an automatic fix task, or only main's failures? Decided: both, deduplicated per test id, as the slice intent says; a flake's fix task marks the flaky list handled so the Overview does not ask twice.

problem:
Night of 2026-10-26/27 (operator's :8000 Hub, read with a mode=ro SQLite query on 2026-10-27):
- Slice B's T1 (task-8618731d065d) was approved by QA but the Hub refused the approval from about 00:44 until 03:39 (about 2 h 55 min) because check run chk-03b0cd6c1cea (started 00:16) failed `hub-tests` on one test, `test_turn_starts_never_freeze_the_hub.py::test_a_turn_start_that_creates_its_checkout_never_stalls_the_loop`. Its narrowed rerun reproduced (confirmed.how 'tests', 29.0 s, run with the gate's own `-n auto` since narrowed_command keeps the options), and the same check failed on main 91b59b5 (on_main exit 1), so the refusal said 'fails on main too' and held the approval for the operator, who was asleep. The same test had already flaked on T1's previous run chk-cd85df778d96 (23:42; failed, passed on the narrowed rerun). T2-T4 depend on T1's approval, so the whole slice waited. T1 finally landed at 03:39 with no override_reason: only after the fix task was approved at 03:24 and main moved to 8ddfe38, whose check run passed.
- The fix task task-eecc162f6e1d ('... fails under the full suite (and on main)') was created by QA's run at 00:43 outside any flow (loop_id null, priority high); the mender moved it pending -> assigned at 01:24; nothing was queued for its assignee until the mender messaged DeveloperOpus2 at 02:55:56 (entry-5ad8203ccc90), and the runtime moved it to in_progress at 02:56. The fix took 15 minutes; the wait 91.
Why the code behaves this way: the main baseline records only the exit code of the whole check on main (project_checks.py:724-726), so 'fails on main too' means 'this check fails on main', not 'these tests fail on main'; a check whose failures are all main's is held for the operator (requirement_gate.py:1124-1128, :1351-1352) and only the operator may approve over failing checks (task_transition_service.py:908-913); the review briefing tells the reviewer to send such a task back (review_turn.py:560-567), contradicting the gate; and nothing starts an assigned task outside a flow: create_task_for_actor commits and broadcasts only (api/v1/tasks.py:868-899), and the stall sweep looks only at in_progress tasks (stalls.py:718).

requirements.rationale: Today any failure of the same check on main counts (project_checks.py:724-726), so a task that breaks test A while main breaks test B is held for the operator instead of sent back, and a landing automated on that answer would land a regression.
requirements.statement: A check's failure counts as main's only when every pytest node id that failed on the task's merged commit (after its serial rerun) also fails when exactly those ids are run with the same serial command on main at the commit the check run was cut from; a failing id that passes there is the task's own and the task goes back to its builder; exit codes and failure counts are never compared.

requirements.rationale: The night's test passed its narrowed rerun once and failed it once, each time run with the gate's `-n auto` (narrowed_command keeps the options, test at test_checks_reuse_a_pass_and_confirm_a_failure.py:310); a timing test is measured under load it does not need. One rerun, as today, so a deterministic own failure is never retried into a pass.
requirements.statement: Before a failure is charged to anyone, the failed node ids are run once more on the same tree and nothing else, serially (the command's xdist worker count set to 0 and its distribution options dropped); if they all pass the failure is a flake and the check passes, recorded as flaky with the ids; if any fails again it stands and is compared with main.

requirements.rationale: Night of 2026-10-26/27: QA's approval of T1 waited 2 h 55 min for an operator who was asleep, and three dependent tasks with it, over a failure the task did not cause.
requirements.statement: When every failure in the task's check run for the work approval would merge is main's or a flake, and the project's automatic override is on, an approval by an actor the mover rules otherwise permit (a reviewer's run or the operator) lands the task with no reason typed; the approval transition records override_by 'hub' and an override_reason naming each check and test id, whether it fails on main or passed on its own, the check run id, the main commit sha, and the fix task; the transition's actor stays the approver.

requirements.rationale: A test the task touched is the task's to make pass even if main is red; a fix task that did not fix its test would otherwise land itself over the very failure it was filed for.
requirements.statement: An override is never automatic for: a failing id that passes on main; a failing or flaky test whose file is among the paths the task's merged work changes against the run's main commit; on a Hub-filed fix task, the ids it was filed for; a check whose failures pytest did not name in full (a non-pytest check, a timeout, a truncated summary, more than 50 failures, a command that cannot be narrowed); or a run with no main answer. Each keeps today's answer: sent back to its builder, or held for the operator where the whole check fails on main too.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap slice D later decides this per gate level; until then the operator needs one switch.
requirements.statement: Each project has a setting, on by default for new and existing projects and shown with the project's checks in the app's settings, that turns off both the automatic override and the fix-task filing; off, approval over main's failures or flakes behaves exactly as before this change (held for the operator, who lands it with a typed reason).

requirements.rationale: On 2026-10-27 the fix task existed only because QA wrote one; it was filed when the run ended rather than at approval, which is also when the flow's agents were idle waiting on T1.
requirements.statement: When a check run ends with a failure that is main's or a flake and the setting is on, the Hub files one fix task naming the check, the test ids, the kind (fails on main / flaky), the main commit, the check run and its failure excerpt; where an open Hub-filed fix task already names every one of those ids nothing new is filed and the override names that task; a flake's fix task also marks the project's flaky-test list handled with that task.

requirements.rationale: Pending tasks are ordered oldest first today (scheduler.py:610-614), so a task filed mid-flow waits behind every pending task of the slice; spec-materialised tasks are all medium (spec_tasks.py:415), so a spec flow's own order does not change.
requirements.statement: A fix task found by a task of a live flow is filed in that flow with priority critical, and a flow's queue orders its pending tasks by priority (critical, high, medium, low) before age, so the next firing staffs the fix task ahead of every other pending task, and the board names the same current item; found by a task outside a live flow, the fix task is filed pending and unassigned.

requirements.rationale: review_turn.py:560-567 tells the reviewer to end with revision_needed for any failed run, which already contradicts the gate's F605 wording for main's failures.
requirements.statement: A reviewer briefed on a task whose failing checks are all main's or flakes is told they are not the task's work, that approving lands it with an override the Hub records, and which fix task covers them; it is not told to send the task back.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-27: task-eecc162f6e1d was moved to assigned at 01:24 and nothing was queued for its assignee until the mender messaged it at 02:55.
requirements.statement: A task that belongs to no flow and is in status assigned, whose assignee is an open agent and whose prerequisites are met, gets one turn queued for that assignee naming and bound to the task, within seconds of entering assigned (created there, moved there, or given a new assignee while there), started as soon as the agent is idle; a turn already queued, delivered or running for that task and assignee since it entered assigned means nothing new is queued.

The stall sweep (every 300 s) queues the same turn for any task left assigned outside a flow with no turn queued or delivered for its assignee since it entered assigned, such as one assigned before this change, while the Hub was down, or whose prerequisites have since cleared.
The task's story in the app shows an automatic override as the Hub's, with its reason, distinct from an operator's override, which keeps reading as the operator's.

in_scope: Deciding by pytest node id whether a failure is main's, a flake, or the task's own
The confirmation rerun made serial (only the failed ids, xdist off) and the main comparison made with the same command
Approval landing over failures that are not the task's, recorded on the transition as the Hub's override
The cases where an override is never automatic
A project setting, on by default, that turns the automatic override and fix-task filing off
The Hub filing one fix task per set of failing tests, deduplicated, at the head of the task's live flow
Pending tasks in a flow's queue ordered by priority before age
The reviewer's briefing saying such failures are not the task's

summary: When the only failing checks on a task's work are failures that are not the task's -- the same test ids fail on main at the commit the check run was cut from, or the failing tests pass when rerun on their own -- approving the task lands it without the operator: the approval transition records an override the Hub made itself (who: the Hub; what: each check, test id, check run and the main commit), and the Hub files one fix task for those tests at the head of the running flow, so the next free agent fixes main while the slice goes on. 'The same failure' is decided by pytest node ids compared like for like (one serial rerun of only the failed ids on the task's tree, then the same serial command on main), never by exit codes or counts, and an override is never automatic for a failure the task introduced or could have (a test passing on main, a test file the task changed, the ids a fix task was filed for, a check whose failures pytest did not name). A project setting, on by default, turns it off. Separately, a task moved to `assigned` outside any flow gets a turn queued for its assignee at once, with the stall sweep as backstop, instead of waiting for someone to message the agent.
